findings: Prefix includes the initial state and every successor; pathLaw is independently defined as the delta-start product of transition weights.

mass and g are defined by statewise transport, not by a path-overlap expression. mass_eq_endpoint_sum and pathLaw_geometric prove their connection to whole prefix trajectories; BC_eq_path_overlap then identifies computed BC with the actual path-law overlap.
hellingerSquared is independently one half the sum of squared square-root differences; hellinger is its nonnegative square root. Neither definition mentions BC or g. No target equality is assumed.

The exact four-clause endpoint proves the squared-distance identity and both distance formulas, including the explicit sum of g. Nonnegativity of the radicand follows from the proven sum-of-squares identity.

prefix_marginal proves that summing out any normalized future suffix gives the stated shorter prefix law, closing the marginal interpretation used in the thesis.
